rows.uncertainty: Diagnosis: [not an IGH study]; mixed leucoderma (segmental, generalized and mixed vitiligo, halo naevi, piebaldism, naevus depigmentosus), a Module 5-damage-repair lead (cell transplantation precedent with long follow-up) entered at Gate A; it says nothing directly about IGH spots. [Module 5-damage-repair is not an allowed module in tools/ledger.py, so the row is filed under 1-hypopigmentation with an ADJACENT diagnosis, as mulekar2007 and lin2024 are.] Retrospective single-centre series [centre inferred from the author affiliation, Ghent University Hospital]; no comparator. The Objectives list 33 + 33 + 6 + 11 + 3 + 1 = [87] patients ('including', so the list may not be exhaustive), but only 82 have imaging results and 54 answered the questionnaire; how the 82 and the 54 overlap, and why the rest are missing, is not in abstract. Number of grafting sessions per patient, any adjunct phototherapy after grafting, and the follow-up range for the imaging result are not in abstract, so time from the FINAL treatment cannot be derived; 'after treatment' and 'mean follow-up' are counted from the transplantation [presumably the first or only grafting, not stated]. Patients said final repigmentation was reached a mean of 10 months post-treatment, so [some imaging assessments at a mean of 15 months may fall near the end of the repigmentation phase]. Abstract states the background that the technique 'was introduced in 1992' [general background, not a result]. Colour match was judged by patients on a questionnaire, not measured by instrument; the authors conclude 'a perfect colour match was seldom obtained'. '71% of patients' does not state its denominator; it is assumed to be the 82 patients with imaging [not stated]. More than 75% repigmentation is partial repigmentation, not complete coverage or colour match.
